title: observability: token/KV cost & latency dashboard + alert tuning
author: Arjun Mehta
description: Context: production workloads showed periodic token-level cost spikes and increased tail latencies for some model/route combinations. This PR adds token-level KV cache metrics, a cost-per-token breakdown by model and route, updated tracing spans to correlate tokens -> requests, and a Grafana dashboard + tuned alert rules to detect regressions early. Motivation: allow platform and SRE to identify cost regressions and cache inefficiencies (KV miss storms) and to tune autoscaling/batching policies proactively. What this PR does: 1) Exposes new Prometheus metrics: redwood_token_request_count, redwood_token_cost_total, redwood_token_latency_ms_bucket, redwood_kv_cache_hit_count, redwood_kv_cache_miss_count, redwood_kv_cache_miss_cost_total. 2) Adds tracing annotations so a token-level trace can be associated with a parent request and model version (span tags: request_id, model_name, model_version, route, token_index). 3) Introduces a new Grafana dashboard (token_kv_cost_latency.json) with panels for token cost-by-model, P50/P95/P99 token latency, KV hit/miss rates, and route-level cost heatmap. 4) Implements alert rules (token_kv_alerts.yaml) tuned for: sustained token_cost_rate spikes, kv_cache_miss_rate > 2% sustained for 5m, token tail latency P95 > target per model for 10m. 5) Adds migration script and config flags (feature flag observability_kv_dash_v2) to rollout gradually (canary 10% for 6h -> 100% over 24h). 6) Docs: updates docs/observability/token_metrics.md and console guide for the dashboard/alert playbook. Testing and rollout: unit/integration tests added for metrics aggregation, manual QA run against perf-canary environment, and a staged rollout plan was used. Rollout notes: enabled behind feature flag; can be rolled back by toggling observability_kv_dash_v2 and by reverting the Grafana dashboard import. Backwards compatibility: metrics are additive; no breaking changes to existing dashboards. Checklist: - [x] Add Prometheus metrics and exporters - [x] Instrument traces at token-level (non-blocking spans) - [x] Grafana dashboard + JSON export - [x] Alert rules with tuned thresholds and runbooks - [x] Integration tests and CI green - [x] Docs and rollout plan
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial metrics + exporter (metrics.go + prometheus exporter), tracing annotations and small API to attach token spans, dashboard JSON + grafana metadata, alerting rules (yaml), doc updates and helm values for feature flag, fixup: alert threshold adjustments after review.
review_comments: Maya Chen: LGTM overall. Left two small nits about metric naming (prefer _total for counters) and a comment about spellings in dashboard panel titles.
Ethan Brooks: Please add an integration test that simulates KV miss storm and verifies alert fires. Also asked to lower the initial kv miss threshold to 2% from 5% to catch early regressions.
Arjun Mehta (author): responded - added integration test and adjusted alert threshold to 2%; fixed metric naming to use _total where appropriate and updated dashboard titles.
Lina Torres: Verified dashboard panels in perf-canary and validated that token -> request tracing shows up in Jaeger with request_id and token_index tags. Approved after QA verification.
ci_checks: integration tests: initial run failed (flaky), re-run -> pass
merge_outcome: Merged via squash by Maya Chen. Merge notes: squashed 6 commits; adjusted git commit message to include Linear ENG-4382 and release notes. No conflicts. Deployed dashboard import to grafana-canary and to prod via automated provisioning after flag rollout.
release_notes:
- Added token-level cost and latency metrics (per-model, per-route).
- New Grafana dashboard: Token KV cost & latency heatmaps and token tail-latency panels.
- New alert rules tuned for token_cost_rate spikes, KV cache miss storms, and token-level tail latency regressions.
- Token-level tracing annotations to link tokens to requests for faster RCA.
- Feature-flagged rollout (observability_kv_dash_v2) with canary deployment.
